title: Review of c27's ringswim cut-repair finding on fresh seed 5: replicated. 2/2 mature swimmers survive a 40% front cut, re-close their link ring (closure >= 0.9 by +100 steps), regain pre-cut area by +220/+320 and swim on (3.95/3.28 BL), and ring-only erasure kills 2/2 by +80 while every twin lives
summary: labkit re-run of c28's world.py on fresh seed 5 (pack/, 256^2, t=10000): 30-100 walled cells, 339 splits / 263 merges. c27's twinrepair.py (run beside a copy of c28's world.py) on seed 5 at T0=10000 for 3000 steps picked cells 15 and 31 (area 248/268, aspect 1.15/1.12, moving). Front cut, the 40% of pixels furthest along the motion (cell 15: 40% of the area, 49% of the links, 46% of the catalyst). Cell 15: ring closure 0.51 -> 0.95 by +120, ring >= 1.5 in 100% of second-half frames, back to pre-cut area by +220, swims 3.95 BL (twin 2.07). Cell 31: closure >= 0.9 by +100, area back by +320, 3.28 BL (twin 0.98). Ring-only damage (links set to 0 in the cell and its wall, shape and catalyst kept): both cells are lost by +80 steps while their exact twins live (s5/twinrepair.png). One caveat from the images: after repair the followed pieces grow well past their twins (cell 15 ends at area 820 vs 390), partly by merging with neighbours, so 'area back' late in the window is not only regrowth.

observations.R: s5/twinrepair.png and s5/result.json: front cut on cells 15 and 31, ring closure >= 0.9 at +100, pre-cut area back at +220/+320, swim 3.95/3.28 BL; ring-only erasure lost at +80 (2/2); twins never lost

seeds_run.result: pass (2/2 front cuts repaired, 2/2 ring-only erasures fatal)

controls_run.R: exact branched undamaged twins for every cut in s5/; ring-only erasure arm

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, 2 cells; wound reset to bath S (world.damage), not the KEEP_S variant. Late in the window the followed pieces merge with neighbours, so area recovery past ~+500 mixes regrowth with fusion. The ring re-forms by the chi drift of the cell's own links, so the ring's reshaping is quasi-equilibrium and by construction; what the cut tests is that the cell keeps making links.
